headline: Sagamore Bridge replacement enters final procurement phase with $956M in federal funding
dek: Massachusetts has authorized the federal grant funding and released the design-build request for proposals, moving the long-delayed Cape Cod crossing closer to construction.
body: Massachusetts officials have moved the Sagamore Bridge replacement into its final procurement phase after securing authorization for $956 million in federal grant funding and releasing the project’s design-build request for proposals on Sept. 28.

The request seeks a team to design and build two new bridge spans, along with reconstructed roadway interchanges and improvements to local and regional traffic movement. The Massachusetts Department of Transportation expects final proposals in May 2027, a public bid opening in July and a notice to proceed late that year.

Construction is expected to begin in winter 2027, according to the state. The project is being led by MassDOT in partnership with the Federal Highway Administration and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, which owns the Sagamore and Bourne bridges. Both existing spans are 91 years old and are the only roadway connections between Cape Cod and the mainland.

MassDOT expects the new eastbound span to open in 2033. Officials say traffic will remain two lanes in each direction during construction, with vehicles shifting to the new eastbound span while the existing bridge is demolished and the westbound span is built.

The Sagamore project is the first phase of a broader Cape Cod Bridges Program that also calls for replacing the Bourne Bridge. MassDOT and the Army Corps have applied for more than $1 billion in federal funding for that second crossing, but that application remains under review.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Sagamore Bridge replacement moves toward construction with $956M federal award
seoDescription: Massachusetts released the final design-build request for proposals for the Sagamore Bridge replacement after securing authorization for $956 million in federal funding.
